source.market_name: Will North Korea invade South Korea before 2027?

market_name: Will North Korea invade South Korea before 2027?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the probability jump coincides with any wire headlines (Yonhap, Reuters) on DMZ incidents, missile launches, or troop movements; confirm EWY/overnight KOSPI futures direction.
time_plan.1h: Compare EWY move to broad EM/ACWI to isolate Korea-specific component; check USD/KRW and CDS spreads for corroboration.
time_plan.2h: Assess whether the signal is persisting or mean-reverting; look for official statements from Seoul, Pyongyang, or US forces Korea.
time_plan.6h: Re-evaluate whether any public confirmation emerged; if nothing credible, treat the market move as noise and expect EWY reversion.
time_plan.12h: Mark final EWY return vs entry; document whether probability spike preceded any public news (leak hypothesis) or faded.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of a North Korean invasion would signal rising Korean-peninsula war risk. The most direct liquid public-market proxy is Korean equity exposure. A genuine escalation scare would trigger foreign capital flight, risk-premium repricing, and a sell-off in EWY. However, the baseline probability of this tail event is extremely low, so only a large, information-driven probability spike (not noise) would translate into a meaningful equity move; most moves in this illiquid, long-dated market are noise and will not move assets at all.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check USD/KRW spot and NDF moves against DXY to see if KRW is underperforming peers.
time_plan.1h: Cross-check with JPY and gold for a coherent risk-off signal; look for Bank of Korea or MOF commentary.
time_plan.2h: Determine if won weakness is Korea-specific or dollar-wide; fade if purely macro.
time_plan.6h: Re-check for any official escalation confirmation; absent news, expect reversion.
time_plan.12h: Record final USD/KRW move and whether it tracked the prediction-market signal.

predictions.reasoning: Escalation fears would drive safe-haven flows out of the won into USD/JPY, pushing USD/KRW higher. FX often reacts faster than equities to geopolitical risk. But the won is also driven by global dollar and rate dynamics, so exposure is diluted; a modest probability move would be swamped by macro factors. Only a credible, large escalation signal would produce the 700bp+ move needed for tradability, which is unlikely from this noisy long-dated market.

evidence_used: Market question concerns a binary North Korea invasion of South Korea before 2027
Korean peninsula risk maps most directly to Korean equity (EWY) and the won (USD/KRW)
Long-dated, low-base-rate tail market where most probability movement is likely noise
uncertainty_notes: Base rate of invasion is extremely low; most probability moves are liquidity/noise, not information
12h window is short for a multi-year resolution market, so asset passthrough is weak unless tied to live escalation news
Proxies EWY and KRW are also driven by global macro (dollar, rates, EM flows), diluting signal
Threshold of 700bps is unlikely to be met absent a genuine, publicly-confirmed escalation

llm_justification.summary: A sharp rise in the implied probability of a North Korean invasion of South Korea would most directly imply risk-off moves in Korean assets: EWY (South Korea equity ETF) lower and the won weaker (USD/KRW higher). However, this is a long-dated, low-base-rate tail market where almost all probability movement is noise rather than leaked information. Only a large, news-corroborated spike would produce tradable (>700bps) moves, which is improbable within a 12h window. Confidence is modest and directional conviction hinges on whether any genuine escalation headline accompanies the market move.
key_assumptions: A meaningful probability spike reflects genuine escalation risk rather than thin-market noise
Korean equity and FX are the fastest, most liquid channels for peninsula-risk repricing
Global macro conditions remain roughly stable so the Korea-specific signal is detectable
failure_modes: The probability move is pure noise in an illiquid long-dated market and no asset moves
Any escalation news is already public and priced, so no fresh asset reaction
EWY/KRW moves are dominated by dollar/EM macro, making the geopolitical signal undetectable
Direction reverses as markets dismiss a false-alarm incident within hours
The 700bps tradability threshold is never reached, rendering the signal non-actionable
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
